calls.thesis: Stance softens from BUY to HOLD: he is sticking with SoFi but says he is not a big buyer at this valuation. He sold around $20 in January and bought back around $15 for 6,000 shares (down ~7% on this leg). Growth still beats legacy banks (35% revenue, 59% earnings expected this year) and the shares trade at ~1.9x book, cheaper than the 3-4x at the start of the year; if book grows 20% a year the multiple falls toward ~1.4x. Rate rises are the headwind for banks and he does not expect a big upside surprise on Tuesday.
calls.price_at_call: Bought back around $15; ~1.9x price-to-book; analyst average target $20 (~39% upside), low target $15; he expects it back over $20 over the next year

calls.thesis: Back in on a second leg and sticking with the shares: SoFi recently became the first national bank to go live with stablecoin settlement across Mastercard's payments network (captions: 'global patent payments network'), which he thinks the market overlooked; instant settlement frees bank capital. Expects it past $20 over the next year, toward past 2x book value from ~1.8x now.
calls.price_at_call: Bought back in at $15.89; ~1.8x price-to-book; target past $20

calls.thesis: Compelling valuation after multiple compression: P/B fell from ~5 (Sep 2025) to ~1.8 vs big banks ~2x, while revenue is up 41% YoY (35% member CAGR since 2023, 15.8M members, cross-sell runway).
32% expected revenue growth at 0.69x PEG - "a great deal"; prime winner as AI agents move lazy deposits to 4.5% SoFi Plus accounts.
calls.bull: Deposit-share wave accelerates as agentic banking goes mainstream.
calls.bear: Valuation still 1.85x book; fintech selloff resumes.
